content.comment_body: Good morning, I need to build a totalizer for a 4-20mA input. After processing the signal and calculating the flow rate in liters per second, I want to sum and save these values so the data is retained even if the device loses power. Is this achievable? Thank you.
Yes, this can be done. I've attached an example demonstrating a similar functionality.
Thank you. If I restart the controller, does the accumulated sum reset?

If the [product_name] controller stops due to manual intervention or power failure, the values will remain stored. Retentivity is enabled in blocks B008 and B013. However, if you update or reload the program, the stored values will be lost.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are exploring how to implement a totalizer that calculates and stores summed values from a 4-20mA input, ensuring persistence even after power cycles. Initial questions about retaining data after restarts are resolved by explaining that enabling retentivity in certain function blocks ensures data is preserved unless the program itself is modified or reloaded.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants the device to reliably maintain cumulative recorded values across power cycles and standard restarts, without requiring special intervention.
